Dear Parents,

We are delighted to announce HUMANVERSE, an inter-house Humanities Fest where our learners will showcase their understanding of Past, Places and People through inquiry, creativity and collaboration.

Key Dates

22 and 23 October: Topic allotment and preparation begins.

2 and 3 November: House-wise selection rounds.

6 November: Fest Day, featuring the winning group from each House.

How will HUMANVERSE work?

Learners will work in section-wise groups within their respective Houses. Topics will be allotted through a draw of lots. Groups will then decide how best to present their learning through models, artefacts, charts, maps, timelines, demonstrations, role-plays, or interactive displays.

Learners will work collaboratively on their projects during the time allocated for preparation at school by their Humanities teacher. They may also discuss their ideas and rehearse their presentations at home.

During the selection rounds, groups will be assessed on Learner preparation list

Learner Preparation Checklist

As learners prepare, they should ensure of the below rubrics:

Knowledge & Accuracy: Explain their topic using accurate information.
Connections & Thinking: Explain how and why things changed, developed or are connected.
Display & Creativity: Use resources that bring their learning to life.
Presentation & Communication: Explain ideas in their own words and respond to questions confidently.
Teamwork & Participation: Contribute actively and ensure every group member participates.

How can parents support?

We warmly encourage you to discuss your child’s topic, help them identify reliable sources and listen as they rehearse their presentation. Please ensure that the research, models and presentations remain the children’s own work.

We encourage every learner to participate enthusiastically and make the most of this opportunity to explore, create, collaborate, and confidently share their learning.

We look forward to your encouragement and support in making HUMANVERSE a meaningful and memorable experience for our Grade 5 learners.

Warm regards,
Grade 5 Humanities Team

HUMANVERSE at a Glance

Theme: HUMANVERSE
Participants: Grade 5 learners
Format: House-wise, group-based participation
Humanities strands: Past | Places | People
House-wise selection round: 2, 3 and 4 November 2026
Fest Day (final showcase): 6 November 2026

How HUMANVERSE Will Work: Step by Step

Step 1: Forming House-wise groups

Learners will work collaboratively in groups within their own Houses. Every learner will be given a role and an opportunity to participate and contribute to the group presentation.

Step 2: Topic selection by draw of lots (from 23 October 2026)

To keep the process fair and transparent, each group will pick a chit and take up the topic written on it. All topics are connected to one of the three strands: Past, Places or People. The full list of topics is given below.

Step 3: Research, planning and preparation (23 October – 1 November 2026)

Groups will research, plan and creatively present their topic. They may use models, artefacts, charts, maps, timelines, demonstrations, role-plays and interactive displays to bring their learning to life. We request learners to begin preparing right away and to keep the judging rubric in mind at every stage, as this is exactly how their work will be assessed.

Step 4: House-wise Selection Round – 2, 3 & 4 November 2026

All groups will present their projects during the House-wise Selection Round on 2, 3, and 4 November 2026. A panel of external judges will evaluate each presentation using the HUMANVERSE rubric given below. The best-performing group from each House will be declared the House Winner.

Important: All students are expected to be present on 2, 3, and 4 November 2026, as these are the scheduled selection dates. No student should be absent on these days. Please plan your commitments accordingly and ensure your availability for the selection round.

Step 5: Fest Day (6 November 2026)

The winning group from each House will present its HUMANVERSE project on Fest Day.

HUMANVERSE Topics (allotted by draw of lots) The topics given below are the ones students will work on in their respective class House groups.

1. PAST – The Human Journey Through Time

Topic

	

Central idea / journey to showcase

	

What learners can display or create




1. From Stone to Smart: The Evolution of Human Life

5B - Draco

	

Late Stone Age → Bronze Age → Iron Age → Industrial Age → Digital/AI Age. Compare homes, clothing, food, occupations, transport, communication and daily life.

	

Large timeline, miniature settlements, artefact replicas, then-and-now charts, interactive "Which Age?" station




2. From Stone Tools to Smart Technology

5B - Tarus

	

Trace how tools changed from stone and microliths → copper → bronze → iron → machines → modern technology. Explain how each development solved human problems.

	

Tool replicas/models, chronological display, invention cards, "Then vs Now" demonstrations




3. From Village to City: How Settlements Changed

5A - Aquila

	

Hunter-gatherer camps → farming villages → Bronze Age towns → ancient cities → modern cities. Focus on why people settled, food surplus, specialist jobs, trade and organisation.

	

3D settlement models showing stages of growth, population arrows, occupation cards




4. From Barter to Global Trade

5A - Tarus

	

Early exchange → Bronze Age trade in copper/tin → coins/money → ships and trade routes → imports/exports → modern global trade.

	

Trade-route maps, barter role-play, ancient goods, coin/currency replicas, modern product journey




5. From Marks to Messages: The Story of Communication

5E - Draco

	

Rock art/symbols → early writing → manuscripts → printing → telephone → internet/digital communication. Explore how communication changed societies.

	

Communication timeline, writing samples, clay-tablet model, message challenge




6. Archaeologist for a Day: How Do We Know About the Past?

5E - Leo

	

Learners investigate how artefacts, pottery, tools, graves, jewellery, buildings and monuments provide evidence about the past.

	

Mini archaeological dig, evidence trays, mystery artefacts, Claim–Evidence–Reasoning (CER) cards

 

2. PLACES – One Planet, Different Worlds

Rather than simply making posters titled "Tundra", "Desert" or "Rainforest", learners will investigate why environments are different and how living things adapt to them.

Topic

	

Central idea / journey to showcase

	

What learners can display or create




2. One Planet, Four Extreme Biomes

5B - Aquila

	

Compare Tropical Rainforest, Desert, Taiga and Tundra. Investigate climate, rainfall, plants, animals and adaptations.

	

Four 3D biome boxes/dioramas, climate cards, touch-and-match adaptation game




3. Built to Survive: Amazing Adaptations

5A – Draco

5A - Leo

	

Investigate how plants and animals survive different environments, such as water storage in deserts, drip-tip leaves in rainforests, and thick fur/fat in cold regions.

	

Adaptation models, "Guess My Biome" cards, animal/plant matching challenge




4. Latitude: The Invisible Lines That Help Explain Our World

5E - Tarus

	

Use the Equator, Tropics and Polar Circles to investigate where major climates and biomes are found, connecting location with environmental patterns.

	

Giant world map/floor map, string latitude lines, coordinate challenge, biome markers




5. A Biome Under Pressure: Then, Now and Tomorrow

5E - Aquila

	

Choose one biome and investigate its natural features, how people use it, threats such as deforestation or climate change, and ways it can be protected.

	

Before/now/future model, conservation solution wall, cause-and-effect chain




6.Same Planet, Different Lives

5C - Aquila

	

Compare how people live in two contrasting environments (for example, tropical rainforest and tundra, or desert and rainforest), connecting climate with homes, clothing, food, transport and occupations.

	

Split model, clothing/home models, comparison charts, "Where would you live?" visitor activity

 

 

 

 

 

3. PEOPLE – How Human Communities Evolved

This strand shows that human development is not only about inventions. It is also about money, trade, communities, rights, responsibilities, rules and people's worldviews.

Topic

	

Central idea / journey to showcase

	

What learners can display or create




1. From Local Market to Global Marketplace

5C - Draco

	

Local trade → domestic trade → international trade → imports/exports → today's interconnected world. Compare trade in India and another country.

	

World trade map, product journey, import/export sorting station, mini marketplace




2. The Journey of a Product: How the World Is Connected

5A – Leo

5D - Tarus

	

Follow one everyday object (shirt, chocolate, phone, tea, pencil) from raw material → producer → manufacturing → transport → trade → shop → consumer.

	

Real object at the centre, world map with strings/arrows, producer/consumer cards




3. Needs, Money and Community: Who Helps When Money Is Not Enough?

5D - Draco

	

Explore needs vs wants → income → budgeting → financial difficulty → immediate community support → long-term support.

	

Family-budget challenge, community-help map, NGO/government/community solution cards




4. From Rules to Laws: Building a Fair Community

5C - Tarus

	

Why humans create rules → what happens when rules are broken → how rules become more organised → laws → fairness and responsibility.

	

Mini community/court/council role-play, "Fair or Unfair?" scenarios, visitors vote on proposed rules




5. Rights and Responsibilities: Two Sides of the Same Coin

5B - Leo

	

Explore selected children's rights from the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) and connect each with a responsibility. Example: right to education ↔ responsibility to respect others' learning.

	

Rights tree, balance scale, scenario cards, rights/responsibility matching game




6.Who Shapes the Way I See the World?

5C- Leo

	

Investigate how family → school → community → culture → experiences influence a person's worldview and identity.

	

Identity wheel, community influence web, "What shapes us?" interactive wall




7.Unsung Heroes: Who Gets Recognised and Who Doesn't?

5D - Aquila

	

Investigate why some contributions receive recognition while others are overlooked, and identify people in the community whose work makes an impact.

	

Community-hero gallery, interviews, contribution cards, "Who helps our community?" display

 HUMANVERSE Judging Rubric (used by the external judges on 2 and 3 November 2026)

The same rubric applies to Past, Places and People, so every group is judged fairly whatever topic it draws. Each presentation is marked out of 20: five criteria, each worth 4 marks.

What we are looking for

	

4 – Excellent

	

3 – Very Good

	

2 – Developing

	

1 – Needs More Work




1. Knowledge & Accuracy

	

We show clear, correct and detailed understanding of our topic.

	

We show good understanding with only a few details missing.

	

We show some understanding, but some information is unclear or incorrect.

	

We need to learn and explain more about our topic.




2. Connections & Thinking

	

We clearly explain how and why things changed, developed, adapted or are connected.

	

We explain several good connections.

	

We show a few connections but do not explain them clearly.

	

We mostly give facts without explaining the connections.




3. Display & Creativity

	

Our models, artefacts, maps, charts or activities are creative, clear and strongly support our explanation.

	

Our display is interesting and supports our topic well.

	

Our display has some useful elements but could be clearer.

	

Our display is incomplete or does not clearly support our topic.




4. Presentation & Communication

	

We speak clearly and confidently, explain in our own words and answer questions well.

	

We explain clearly and answer most questions.

	

We need some support to explain our ideas or answer questions.

	

We mostly read from the display or find it difficult to explain our topic.




5. Teamwork & Participation

	

Every group member participates, knows the topic and contributes meaningfully.

	

Almost everyone participates and works well together.

	

Some members participate more than others.

	

Only one or two members do most of the work or presentation.

 

Total: ____ / 20

Dear Learners,

Here are some ideas to help you work on your project topics house-wise. You can use these ideas as a starting point and add your own creative ideas to make your project more interesting, informative, and unique.

Remember, these are just suggestions—feel free to think creatively and add your own ideas to make your topic the best!

 

Aquila – Unsung Heroes: Who Gets Recognised and Who Doesn’t?

Idea: “Heroes We Know & Heroes We Don’t” poster. One side famous people, other side everyday heroes (cleaner, farmer, nurse, parent).
Impact tip: Interview one school staff member and add their photo or quote.

Draco – Needs, Money and Community: Who Helps When Money Is Not Enough?

Idea: Chart showing Needs → What money can buy → Who helps when money is not enough (family, school, community, government).
Impact tip: Give one real local example (mid-day meal, free books, hospital, etc.).

Leo – Built to Survive: Amazing Adaptations

Idea: “Animal Adaptation Cards” – Make 4–5 cards. Each card has a picture of an animal + one adaptation + why it helps.
Impact tip: Choose animals from different biomes (camel, polar bear, cactus, penguin) so it looks varied and colourful.

Tarus – The Journey of a Product: How the World Is Connected

Idea: “Journey of a Chocolate / Mobile Phone / T-shirt” flowchart. Show the steps from raw material → factory → shop → home with simple pictures and arrows.
Impact tip: Highlight 2–3 countries involved so students see global connection clearly.

 

Be creative, work together as a team, and make your project something you are proud to share
